punchline: Elizabeth Gilbert says you can choose to create like a Trickster instead of a Martyr.
thirty_sec: In Big Magic, Elizabeth Gilbert contrasts two creative attitudes. The Martyr believes creativity requires suffering and treats pain as proof of worth. The Trickster works just as hard but with lightness, humor and trust, treating obstacles as part of the game. Gilbert chooses the Trickster, arguing that the suffering myth is harmful and that joy and seriousness can go together.
question: Do you believe good work has to hurt?
